title: Define SLO triggers and release gates for KV-cache regeneration and canary rollback
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Context: Last quarter's KV-cache incident showed that large-scale cache invalidation (regen) events can spike backend token utilization and cause transient request timeouts for low-tier customers. Postmortem action A-4 recommended codifying deterministic triggers and throttles for KV-cache regeneration, adding canary release gates, and embedding synthetic verification into release criteria. This ticket translates those actions into concrete PRD requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout constraints for runtime-1.19.
goals: Specify SLO-based triggers for when automated KV-cache regeneration is allowed to proceed without operator confirmation
Define per-tenant/regional throttles and prefetch sampling to limit regen-induced spike load
Add canary gating rules and rollback thresholds tied to synthetic verification and production telemetry
Provide clear acceptance tests and runbook steps for release readiness and post-deploy checks
out_of_scope: Full redesign of cache eviction heuristics (separate infra initiative)
Persistent storage format changes for KV cache
acceptance_criteria: A1: SLO trigger thresholds documented: regen allowed only if 95th latency < 120ms and backend CPU usage < 70% for 5m window
A2: Regen throttle implemented as token-bucket per-region with default burst=1000 req/min and configurable via runtime config
A3: Prefetch sampling implemented to replay max 1% of live traffic to warm caches during regen; sampling rate adjustable per-customer
A4: Canary release gate: first 5% of capacity receives regen; abort if error rate increases by >1.5x or P95 latency increases by >20% within 10 minutes

A5: Synthetic verification: a suite of 8 synthetic prompts validating cache hits, correctness of responses, and latency is executed automatically post-deploy; must pass 95% of checks before global rollout
A6: Runbook updated with step-by-step rollback and mitigation actions and linked to on-call playbook
A7: Dashboards created: regen-events, per-region regen-rate, synthetic-check-pass-rate, and canary-health with alerting rules configured
tradeoffs_and_notes: Trade-off: aggressive prefetch reduces cold-start cost but increases GPU/utilization and billing; default conservative sampling chosen to limit customer impact
Trade-off: longer canary windows increase safety but delay fixes; chosen window (10 minutes) balances speed vs signal quality
Note: some long-tail customers with batch-heavy workloads may require higher burst allowances; provide tenant-level override API and process for approvals
Note: this PRD relies on ENG tickets ENG-18902 (regen throttling infra) and ENG-19670 (synthetic test harness); any delay there blocks release gating
design_feedback: 2026-03-11 - Marco Liu (ENG): prefer token-bucket over fixed-rate to allow short bursts; updated acceptance A2 to token-bucket semantics
2026-03-11 - Priya Desai (Reliability): request adding a 1-hour cooldown per-tenant after a manual rollback to avoid churn
2026-03-12 - Design (Elena Park): suggested adding a compact canary dashboard tile showing both absolute and relative delta metrics for quick on-call triage
implementation_notes: Implementation will add a runtime config path: /runtime/regen/throttle and /runtime/regen/canary_policy
Require backward-compatible defaults so older private deployments keep current behavior until explicitly enabled
Instrumentation: add regen_event tag to existing traces and expose a regen.duration histogram
risks: If synthetic checks have false negatives, they may block safe rollouts; engineering to ensure diverse prompt coverage
Overly conservative defaults may slow rollout velocity for critical fixes—product team to maintain escalation path
Incorrect tenant overrides could allow a single noisy tenant to trigger cluster-wide regen pressure; need quota checks
